title: Next-Latent Prediction: Beyond Next-Token
hook: Microsoft's NextLat teaches a transformer to predict its own next hidden state, not just the next token - building a compact internal world model and decoding up to 3.3x faster.
key_points: Adds an auxiliary objective: predict the model's own next latent (hidden) state from the current latent and the next token, on top of standard next-token prediction.
Argues next-token prediction alone is 'myopic'; latent prediction pressures the model to form compact internal world models for reasoning and planning.
Enables up to 3.3x faster inference via self-speculative decoding, drafting from the model's own predicted latents.
Acts as a self-supervised add-on that improves representation learning rather than a new architecture.
content_html: Most transformers are trained on a single objective: predict the next token. Microsoft Research argues that's myopic — it never explicitly asks the model to model where it's headed. Their method, Next-Latent Prediction (NextLat), adds a second self-supervised objective on top: predict the model's own next latent (hidden) state, given the current latent state and the next token.
extra_html: The claimed benefits are threefold. First, representation learning improves, because the model must encode information useful for forecasting its own future states. Second, those forecasts encourage compact internal world models that help with reasoning and planning. Third — and concretely — predicting your own next latent enables self-speculative decoding: the model drafts ahead from its predicted latents and verifies in parallel, which the authors report yields up to 3.3x faster inference. NextLat is presented as a training add-on rather than a new architecture. Figures and claims are from the authors' preprint shared on r/MachineLearning; see the source for details.

related.title: World Models Meet Language Models
related.hook: A world model can imagine what happens next; an LLM can reason about it. The hard part is knowing when to trust the daydream — and when the simulation is just plausible nonsense.

related.title: Latent Context Language Models: Compressing the Prompt, Not the Cache
related.hook: Instead of shrinking the KV cache, compress the prompt itself: a small encoder folds a long context into a few latent embeddings that a bigger decoder reads — letting agents skim and expand on demand.

related.title: Speculative Decoding
related.hook: Let a small, fast model guess the next few words, then have the big model check them all in one shot. Same output, fewer slow steps.

flashcards.prompt: What does NextLat predict beyond the next token?
flashcards.back_html: The model's own next latent (hidden) state — given the current latent and the next token — as an auxiliary self-supervised objective layered on top of next-token prediction.

flashcards.prompt: Why does NextLat claim up to 3.3x faster inference?

choices.text: It enables self-speculative decoding from the model's own predicted latents
It quantizes all weights to 4-bit precision
It replaces attention with state-space layers

flashcards.explanation_html: Because the model can forecast its own next latent state, it can draft and verify tokens itself — self-speculative decoding — without a separate draft model.

flashcards.prompt: What problem with plain next-token prediction does NextLat target?
flashcards.back_html: It's "myopic": predicting only the next token doesn't push the model to build the compact internal world models useful for reasoning and planning.
